This Court has heard the arguments and perused the record.
15. Before discussing the testimonies of the witnesses, it would be prudent to briefly discuss the legal position involved in the present case.

The provisions of section 288 IPC is reproduced below :-
IPC Section 288 deals with "Negligent conduct with respect to pulling down or repairing buildings," making it a punishable offense for anyone who, while demolishing or fixing a structure, fails to take adequate precautions to prevent danger to human life from its collapse, punishable by up to six months jail, a fine of 1000, or both, and is a bailable, non-cognizable offense triable by any Magistrate

The provisions of section 304A IPC is reproduced below :-
Whoever causes the death of any person by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
16.
Before proceeding further, it would be relevant to discuss the meaning of expressions 'rash' and 'negligent'.
These words rash and negligent had not been defined in the Indian Penal Code.

However, as per Black's law dictionary, eighth edition the word 'negligent' is characterized by a person's failure to exercise the degree of care that someone of ordinary prudence would have exercised in the same circumstances.

The terminology of criminal negligence has been discussed by Honble Supreme Court in the judgment titled as 'S. N. Hussain vs. State of Andra Pradesh' AIR 1972 SC 685 as under;-
"Criminal negligence on the other hand, is the cross and culpable neglect or failure to exercise that reasonable and proper care and precaution to guard against injury either to the public generally or to an individual in particular, which, having regard all the circumstance out of which the charge has arisen it was the imperative duty of the accused person to have adopted.....

entities.text: S. N. Hussain vs. State of Andra Pradesh' AIR 1972 SC 685
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Culpable negligence lies in the failure to exercise reasonable and proper care and the extent of its reasonableness would always depend upon the circumstances of each case".
Digitally signed by KOMAL KOMAL Date:

In the present case it has been alleged that accused Dinesh and Sarvan Lal had omitted to take such order at the time of repair of building/ house which belongs to accused Sarvan Lal while pulling it down and consequently, death of one Gautam occurred who was working there as a labourer on the date of incident ie 7.4.2013.
18.
On perusal of the testimonies, it is reflected that PW1 Manoj Kumar Singh is the brother of deceased Gautam.
Further, he is not the eye-witness to the incident as he reached the spot after the occurrence of the incident.
Thereafter, PW2 Smt. Gayatri who was wife of the accused has been examined.
The testimony of PW2 reflects that she has admitted that her husband had consumed bhaang on the date of incident.

Further, there are contradiction in her statement as to how she got to know about the incident as in her examination in chief, she has stated that other labourers came to her house to inform her about the incident, however, in her cross-examination, she stated that she saw her husband lying on the ground in unconscious condition when she went to give food to him.
She is also not the eye-witness to the incident.
Further, her testimony fails to describe the specification about the property.

Further, when the photographs ie Ex. P1 has been shown to her,
she has stated that it is correct that those photographs only shows the debris and the address of the site cannot be ascertained by those photographs.
19. Thereafter, PW3 Kundan Singh was examined who identified the dead body of deceased Gautam as he is the cousin brother of the deceased Gautam.

Then, PW4 Santosh was examined who was the co-labourer of the deceased Gautam on the date of incident and he deposed that accused Dinesh and owner of the house Sarvan did not provide the safety helmets to them while they were breaking the house and he further deposed that all of a sudden while they were working, deceased Gautam had fallen down from the said building upon the malva (pathar, rori & bricks, etc.) and blood started oozing from his body.
He further stated that both accused did not take the deceased Gautam to the hospital despite his requests.

sentences.text: 22. It is a settled position of law that whenever there are two views possible, the view which favors the innocence of the accused is to be accepted by the court.
It is settled proposition of law that burden is on the prosecution to prove as how the accused persons are rash and negligent during the repair work of the building/ house.
The judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Mahadeo Hari Lokre vs. State of Maharastra AIR 1972 SC 221 has been relied upon 23.

entities.text: Mahadeo Hari Lokre vs. State of Maharastra AIR 1972 SC 221
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is an established principle of criminal law if prosecution fails to prove its case beyond a reasonable doubt, the accused is entitle to acquittal and Court does not need to consider the defense's case.

The burden of proof is solely on the prosecution to establish the guilt of the accused,
and if they failed to meet this standard, the accused defense becomes irrelevant.
24. In view of the discussion herein above, I hold that the prosecution has failed to establish beyond reasonable doubt that accused persons had been negligent on the date of incident.
Hence, the ingredients of offence punishable under Section 288 IPC are not proved beyond reasonable doubt.

25. Once it is not proved that the accused persons are negligent, it also remained not proved that any rash or negligent act of the accused persons had caused death of the deceased, not amounting to culpable homicide.

To impose criminal liability on the accused for the offence punishable under Section 304A IPC, it is necessary that the death should have been the direct result of a rash and negligent act of the accused Digitally signed by KOMAL KOMAL

9 26.

In the light of the discussion herein above, I am of the opinion that the prosecution has failed to establish that death was occasioned by either rash and/or negligent driving of the vehicle or any negligent act of the accused.
Therefore, benefit of the doubt is given to the accused persons as per law.
Accordingly, accused Denesh Kumar and Sarvan Lal are acquitted of the offences alleged.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
These words rash and negligent had not been defined in the Indian Penal Code.
However, as per Black's law dictionary, eighth edition the word 'negligent' is characterized by a person's failure to exercise the degree of care that someone of ordinary prudence would have exercised in the same circumstances.
The terminology of criminal negligence has been discussed by Honble Supreme Court in the judgment titled as 'S. N. Hussain vs. State of Andra Pradesh' AIR 1972 SC 685 as under;-
"Criminal negligence on the other hand, is the cross and culpable neglect or failure to exercise that reasonable and proper care and precaution to guard against injury either to the public generally or to an individual in particular, which, having regard all the circumstance out of which the charge has arisen it was the imperative duty of the accused person to have adopted.....
In the present case it has been alleged that accused Dinesh and Sarvan Lal had omitted to take such order at the time of repair of building/ house which belongs to accused Sarvan Lal while pulling it down and consequently, death of one Gautam occurred who was working there as a labourer on the date of incident ie 7.4.2013.

Further, the prosecution fails to provide the specification as to the property and to the fact that how deceased Gautam had fallen and sustained injuries and how the act of accused is attributable to the death/ injuries to the deceased.

107/2013, PS Nihal Vihar +0530 Page No. 11 of 13 sufficient to prove the spot of incident and consequently, the rash or negligent act on the part of the accused persons.
22. It is a settled position of law that whenever there are two views possible, the view which favors the innocence of the accused is to be accepted by the court.
It is settled proposition of law that burden is on the prosecution to prove as how the accused persons are rash and negligent during the repair work of the building/ house.
The judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Mahadeo Hari Lokre vs. State of Maharastra AIR 1972 SC 221 has been relied upon 23.
It is an established principle of criminal law if prosecution fails to prove its case beyond a reasonable doubt, the accused is entitle to acquittal and Court does not need to consider the defense's case.
The burden of proof is solely on the prosecution to establish the guilt of the accused,
and if they failed to meet this standard, the accused defense becomes irrelevant.
24. In view of the discussion herein above, I hold that the prosecution has failed to establish beyond reasonable doubt that accused persons had been negligent on the date of incident.
Hence, the ingredients of offence punishable under Section 288 IPC are not proved beyond reasonable doubt.
25. Once it is not proved that the accused persons are negligent, it also remained not proved that any rash or negligent act of the accused persons had caused death of the deceased, not amounting to culpable homicide.
In the light of the discussion herein above, I am of the opinion that the prosecution has failed to establish that death was occasioned by either rash and/or negligent driving of the vehicle or any negligent act of the accused.
